chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Abd al-Malik ibn Utbah al-Hashimi said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who has dinars for some of his partners, so he takes silver coins (dirhams) in their place for his needs, and on the day they were taken, the rate was seven and a half dirhams per dinar. The owner of the money might ask for some of the silver, but it is not present, so the money-changer buys it for him at this rate or similar. Then the rate changes before he settles the account, until the silver becomes twelve dirhams per dinar. Is it permissible for him to do that, given that the original rate on the day they were taken was seven and a half dirhams per dinar? He (peace be upon him) said: 'When he gives him the silver in the number of the dinars, it does not harm him how the exchange is done, so there is no objection.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on currency exchange when the market rate changes before repayment in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the permissibility of currency exchange (sarf) amidst market volatility, establishing that returning the exact count of the original currency type (gold for gold) validates the transaction regardless of subsequent price shifts. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes this from riba by focusing on the physical return of the specific commodity rather than the fluctuating monetary value, a key principle in Shia commercial jurisprudence. This ruling provides practical guidance for merchants and individuals managing debts in unstable economic conditions, ensuring that temporary devaluation or appreciation does not constitute unjust gain.
